metadata.title: FormalPrompt self-hosting specification
metadata.description: Use FormalPrompt's own canvas to review the product boundary, runtime, agent isolation, compilation, and MVP evidence.

tabs.label: Product
tabs.description: Confirm the relationship between the general canvas runtime and its first workflow.

fields.label: General platform
fields.value: Agent Canvas is a local, ephemeral interaction surface that CLI agents can use to present structured visual data, collect rich user input, and return a typed result.

fields.label: Reference application
fields.value: FormalPrompt is the first Agent Canvas workflow: a provenance-aware specification workbench and deterministic handoff compiler.

fields.label: Canonical state
fields.rationale: A single declarative source of truth prevents divergence between UI, chat, and artifacts.

options.label: Versioned canvas document
options.implications: The UI, assistants, validators, and compiler all project from one typed state.

options.label: Conversation transcript
options.implications: Flexible but difficult to validate, diff, and compile deterministically.

assistance.prompt: Compare canonical-state choices for auditability and interoperability.

tabs.label: Runtime
tabs.description: Confirm browser, server, portability, and security decisions.

options.label: Graphical browser
options.implications: Use the installed default browser for desktop users.

options.label: Carbonyl
options.implications: Use Chromium rendering inside terminal and SSH environments.

options.label: URL-only fallback
options.implications: Print the authenticated local URL when no launcher is available.

fields.label: Target host platforms
fields.rationale: A general CLI-agent tool should not assume one host OS.

options.label: Windows
options.implications: Graphical browser is primary; Carbonyl may require WSL or a container.

options.label: macOS
options.implications: Both graphical browser and upstream Carbonyl binaries are plausible.

options.label: Linux
options.implications: Support desktop, headless console, containers, and SSH.

fields.label: Core implementation
fields.rationale: Python is broadly available in agent environments; FastAPI provides a small typed localhost boundary.

options.label: Python and FastAPI
options.implications: Simple agent integration and packaging; semantic static frontend needs no Node runtime.

options.label: Node.js
options.implications: Natural web tooling but adds a JavaScript runtime requirement.

options.label: Rust
options.implications: Excellent binary distribution at greater initial implementation cost.

options.label: Loopback only
options.implications: Remote binding requires an explicit override.

options.label: Local network
options.implications: Requires stronger authentication, TLS, and origin controls.

fields.label: Agent-supplied executable browser code
fields.rationale: Specification canvases should be declarative. Freeform generated presentations need a separate sandbox.

tabs.label: Agents
tabs.description: Define context isolation and authority for facilitator and reviewer processes.

fields.label: Facilitator responsibility
fields.value: Answer field-level questions, explain options and implications, and identify consequential gaps without adding its transcript to the primary execution context.

fields.label: Independent reviewer responsibility
fields.value: Challenge ambiguity, contradictions, hidden assumptions, feasibility, and unverifiable acceptance criteria before user approval.

options.label: JSON stdin/stdout command
options.implications: Provider-neutral, process-isolated, and usable by any CLI agent adapter.

options.label: Embedded model providers
options.implications: Easier initial setup but couples credentials and provider APIs into the core.

fields.label: Can suggestions mutate fields automatically?
fields.rationale: Assistant output remains advisory until the user explicitly applies it.

tabs.label: Delivery
tabs.description: Confirm compiler outputs and the evidence required for the first usable release.

fields.label: Compiled run bundle
fields.value: Canonical JSON specification, readable Markdown specification, compact execution brief, approval record, event journal, content-hash manifest, and machine-readable result.

options.label: Stage inside run directory
options.implications: Project modification becomes a separate explicit operation.

options.label: Write directly into project
options.implications: Convenient but allows generated setup to overwrite user-owned files.

fields.label: MVP acceptance evidence
fields.description: State the exact automated and manual evidence required before calling the reference workflow usable.

assistance.prompt: Propose concrete cross-platform, API, browser, security, and end-to-end acceptance checks.
